Agent Runtime Isolation

By R. Example

20 October 2026

This constructed note argues that runtime isolation is the part of an agent sandbox that carries the security weight. A tool call the model emits is untrusted input, so the sandbox — not the prompt — is what decides which capabilities the call can reach.

The note separates three layers: process boundaries,
filesystem scope, and network egress. Each layer can be enforced without the model cooperating.

  • Process boundaries limit what a tool call can crash.
  • Filesystem scope limits what it can read or write.
  • Network egress limits where it can send data.
Isolation is only meaningful if it holds when the model is wrong.
